article.headline: How much scene memory does a long video need?
article.lead: Honeycomb represents a scene with a fixed-size memory across six planes. Ego2Act evaluates whether a first-person video completes an intended manipulation. A stable background and a correctly completed action ask different things of the same clip.

paragraphs.text: Honeycomb introduces HexMemory, a fixed-size memory representation that efficiently stores scene features across six spatial and spatiotemporal planes. This approach significantly reduces storage requirements during long-horizon video generation, as shown in experiments on WorldScore and RealEstate10K. The model employs a feed-forward writer that processes only new observations, enhancing efficiency without compromising performance. The confidence-weighted pooling mechanism further contributes to robust video generation quality and revisit consistency, addressing the challenges of maintaining coherence in long video sequences.

Ego2Act establishes a benchmark for goal-directed manipulation in egocentric video generation, featuring 2,640 videos across 110 tasks of varying complexity. It includes Ego2ActJudge, a reference-free evaluation pipeline that aligns better with human consensus on task completion compared to existing methods. The study highlights that many current models struggle with executing multi-step actions accurately, leading to incomplete simulations and poor handling of complex physical dynamics.

A comprehensive survey reviews post-training and alignment strategies for video generation models. It categorizes approaches into supervised fine-tuning, self-training and distillation, preference- and reward-based methods, and inference-time techniques. The authors discuss the unique challenges of maintaining temporal coherence and adhering to human intent, while also addressing open challenges like scalable reward design and long-horizon temporal consistency, guiding future research in the field.

The study on distillation dynamics investigates how rollout policy impacts model training. It reveals that token-level KL direction affects task performance and output coverage, with on-policy data enhancing generalization for complex tasks. Where-OPD introduces an on-policy self-distillation method for multimodal large language models, achieving a 3.23-point performance improvement across benchmarks by integrating spatially grounded textual guidance. PyRUA-Lean enhances robot control by using feedback-driven primitive composition, resulting in a 14% increase in task success rate while reducing token usage significantly.
